alex_infra: FYI AcmeFinance (private VPC) reporting ~30% of GPUs failing after a kernel roll to 6.1.0 + NVIDIA driver 530.41. Symptoms: NCCL init errors and cuda driver version mismatch in the inference pods. Short logs below we pulled from one host.

alex_infra: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3d:00: GPU-0fa1b2c3: Loaded the NVIDIA kernel module, but the user-space driver appears to be incompatible.
[ 1234.568000] cuda: failed to initialize: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
[ 1234.569000] nccl: NET/IB: The requested net plugin failed to initialize
```

mira_sre: Which CUDA toolkit package is installed on the hosts? customer is on RHEL8. Do we have `nvidia-smi` output?

alex_infra: nvidia-smi shows: `Driver Version: 530.41.00  CUDA Version: 11.8` but pods are built against CUDA 11.7 runtime. Also `lsmod | grep nv` shows `nvidia 0 0 nv_peer_mem 16384 0`.

ops-bot: :information_source: kernel-rollout-bot: kernel 6.1.0 scheduled to private-onprem group at 2026-03-17T02:00Z (completed on 30 hosts)

jamal_eng: Two potential angles: 1) customer driver package might be custom-built (DKMS) and the module ABI doesn't match the kernel ABI after the roll. 2) NCCL plugin sometimes requires a matching CUDA driver+kernel module; minor CUDA microversions can break the symbol table.

olivia_eng: If nv_peer_mem is present it implies an RDMA plugin is active; try temporarily blacklisting `nv_peer_mem` to see if NCCL falls back to `ib_uverbs`/TCP. Command to test (non-destructive): `sudo modprobe -r nv_peer_mem && sudo systemctl restart kubelet` on a canary node.

andrew_support: Also ask customer to run `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` and `dkms status` — common sign is vermagic mismatch between module and running kernel. If they used a vendor driver CLI it may have rebuilt against the old kernel headers and not the new one.

alex_infra: We have a canary pool of 3 hosts still online. I'll try the `modprobe -r` test on one and report results. If that fails, next step would be driver rollback. Need a safe rollback procedure we can give the customer without rebooting all nodes at once.

jamal_eng: Rollback steps we recommend: 1) Confirm `uname -r` and `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic`. 2) If vermagic mismatches, reinstall matching driver package from our artifact repo: `sudo rpm -Uvh --force /opt/redwood/drivers/nvidia-520.61.05.rpm` (example). 3) `sudo dracut --regenerate-all --force` (RHEL) then reboot canary. Quick check before full rollout: `nvidia-smi` + run a tiny CUDA smoke test inside a container. Also a quick way to detect module/kern mismatch: `grep -i 'Unknown symbol' /var/log/messages`.

mira_sre: Also note: Private/VPC customers sometimes pin a specific driver in their IaC. We should confirm if AcmeFinance runs any custom DKMS modules (intel/oneapi, third-party monitoring) that could conflict. Ask for `rpm -qa | grep -E "nvidia|dkms|kernel-headers"` and the kubelet config for `device-plugin` flags.

andrew_support: I've opened a support ticket with the account team and asked Acme for the `modinfo` and `dkms status` output. Ticket: ACME-9872. They've flagged this as P2 (impacting production).

alex_infra: Quick status: after `modprobe -r nv_peer_mem` on canary, NCCL errors reduced but one pod still reported `cuda driver version mismatch`. Customer had an old `libcuda.so` under `/usr/local/lib` from a previous manual install — probably shadowing the packaged driver. We need to document that in the private deployment compatibility guidance.

jamal_eng: Good catch. Action items: - olivia: draft a KB section about manual library shadowing for private customers - andrew: confirm whether our onboarding script checks for /usr/local/lib/libcuda.* - alex: coordinate rollback/runbook for customer if uninstalling local libs isn't possible.

olivia_eng: I'll draft the KB. Short note: tell customers to run `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` and ensure the path points to `/usr/lib64` from the packaged driver.

alex_infra: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket and paste these diagnostics. Please add any matrix changes (we may need to mark kernel 6.1.0 + driver 530 as "unsupported for private onprem until validated").

ops-bot: :rotating_light: incident created INC-2026-0342 (private-vpc-kernel-compat) — assigned to eng-infra

mira_sre: After KB + matrix update we'll schedule a re-validation window. Preference: after-hours maintenance to reduce customer impact.

alex_infra: Agree. Will sync with customer on maintenance windows and share rollback runbook. :thumbsup:
